summary.en: Use three coordinates for layered data and calculate their row-major positions.
summary.bn: স্তর, সারি ও কলাম দিয়ে ডেটা রাখো; মেমরিতে কোন মানের পরে কোন মান আসে তা হিসাব করো।

notes: Fixed multidimensional arrays use the same nested-array layout in C89 through C23.

sections.title: Add a coordinate when the data needs one
Do not confuse shape with total count

Additional dimensions still use nested arrays
Let each dimension name a real category

examples.title: Two days of two-room readings
examples.explanationHtml: Day zero totals 141 and day one totals 201. Three loops name the meaning of each coordinate.

examples.title: Calculate an element offset
examples.explanationHtml: The last element has offset 23 in a 24-element object. This calculation counts elements rather than assuming an int byte size.

examples.title: Partial initialization of a cube
examples.explanationHtml: Only element [0][0][0] receives 7. The aggregate initializer initializes every other element to zero.

practice.title: Sum every layer
practice.statementHtml: Read layers, rows and columns from 1 to 3, then their product number of ints from -100 to 100 in layer-row-column order. Print Dimensions and entries: first, then each layer total on its own line.
hints: Reset total for each d, outside the row and column loops.

practice.title: Maximum across a volume
practice.statementHtml: Use dimensions 1 to 3 and entries -100 to 100 in layer-row-column order. Print Dimensions and entries: then the largest entry.
hints: Initialize best from cube[0][0][0] after input.

practice.title: Collapse layers into a matrix
practice.statementHtml: Use dimensions 1 to 3 and entries -100 to 100 in layer-row-column order. Print Dimensions and entries: then a rows by columns matrix containing sums across all layers at each coordinate.
hints: For each row and column, accumulate over d.

practice.title: Print the nested traversal order
practice.statementHtml: Use dimensions 1 to 3 and entries -100 to 100 in layer-row-column order. Print Dimensions and entries: then one d r c value line per element in the same traversal order.
hints: Do not flatten the cube with a pointer that crosses row boundaries.

quiz.prompt: How many scalar elements does int a[2][3][4] contain?
quiz.explanation: Multiply all three extents to count the int elements.

quiz.prompt: Which coordinate changes fastest in contiguous three-dimensional storage?
options: The coordinate with the greatest logical value
quiz.explanation: C nests complete row arrays inside layers, so columns are adjacent within each row.

quiz.prompt: A partially initialized two-by-two-by-two cube has which last value?
quiz.explanation: The first scalar is eight; omitted aggregate elements become zero.

quiz.prompt: What element offset locates a[d][r][c] in a[D][R][C]?
quiz.explanation: The formula counts earlier complete layers, then rows, then columns.

quiz.prompt: Can a valid layer index compensate for an excessive column index?
options: Yes, if total offset is small
No, every subscript has its own bound
quiz.explanation: Each nested array access must stay inside its own selected subarray.

quiz.prompt: The offset of coordinate one, one, two in a two-by-three-by-four shape is what?
quiz.explanation: Twelve earlier-layer elements, four earlier-row elements and two columns give eighteen.

quiz.prompt: Where should a per-layer sum be reset?
options: Inside the layer loop before its row traversal
quiz.explanation: The accumulator should include one entire layer and no preceding layer.

quiz.prompt: When is dense three-dimensional storage a reasonable choice?
options: A few isolated entries among enormous dimensions
Regular data with useful values at most coordinate combinations
Unequal row lengths without an explicit plan
quiz.explanation: Dense rectangular storage reserves every coordinate combination, which suits regular filled data.

quiz.prompt: A layer collapse adds matching coordinates. Which pair appears?
quiz.explanation: The first coordinate sums two and five; the second sums three and seven.

quiz.prompt: If physical storage is cube[3][3][3] but logical columns is one, what is the physical row width?
quiz.explanation: A logical used bound does not resize the declared row type.

quiz.prompt: What output shape results from summing all layers at each row-column coordinate?
quiz.explanation: Collapsing the layer coordinate leaves row and column coordinates.

keyPoints.en: A three-dimensional array groups matrices into layers.
keyPoints.bn: ত্রিমাত্রিক অ্যারেতে একাধিক ম্যাট্রিক্স স্তর হিসেবে থাকে।

keyPoints.en: The rightmost index changes fastest in contiguous storage.
keyPoints.bn: পরপর মেমরিতে ডানদিকের ইনডেক্সটি সবার আগে বদলায়।

keyPoints.en: For a[D][R][C], the element offset is (d*R+r)*C+c.
keyPoints.bn: a[D][R][C]-তে উপাদানের দূরত্ব (d*R+r)*C+c দিয়ে পাওয়া যায়।

keyPoints.en: Each dimension has its own independent index bound.
keyPoints.bn: প্রতিটি মাত্রার ইনডেক্সের জন্য আলাদা সীমা আছে।

keyPoints.en: A layer subtotal resets once per layer.
keyPoints.bn: প্রতিটি স্তরের শুরুতে সেই স্তরের যোগফল নতুন করে শুরু হয়।

keyPoints.en: Dense multidimensional arrays suit regular rectangular data.
keyPoints.bn: নিয়মিত আয়তাকার ডেটায় ঘন বহুমাত্রিক অ্যারে কাজে লাগে।

examQuestions.question: Derive the scalar element offset of a[d][r][c] in int a[D][R][C].
examQuestions.answerHtml: There are d earlier layers with R*C elements each, then r earlier rows with C elements each, then c earlier columns. The offset is d*R*C+r*C+c, equivalently (d*R+r)*C+c. Multiply by sizeof(int) only for a byte offset. Each coordinate still needs its own valid bound.

#include <stdio.h>



int main(void)
{
    int a[2][2][2] = {{{8}}};
    printf("%d %d\n", a[0][0][0], a[1][1][1]);
    return 0;
}

8 0

The first scalar is eight; omitted aggregate elements become zero.

examQuestions.question: Use dimensions 1 to 3 and entries -100 to 100 in layer-row-column order. Print Dimensions and entries: then one d r c value line per element in the same traversal order.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>



int main(void)
{
    int layers, rows, columns;
    int cube[3][3][3];
    puts("Dimensions and entries:");
    if (scanf("%d%d%d", &layers, &rows, &columns) != 3 ||
        layers < 1 || layers > 3 || rows < 1 || rows > 3 || columns < 1 || columns > 3) {
        return 1;
    }
    for (int d = 0; d < layers; d++) {
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < columns; c++) {
                if (scanf("%d", &cube[d][r][c]) != 1 || cube[d][r][c] < -100 ||
                    cube[d][r][c] > 100) {
                    return 1;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    for (int d = 0; d < layers; d++) {
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < columns; c++) {
                printf("%d %d %d %d\n", d, r, c, cube[d][r][c]);
            }
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

Do not flatten the cube with a pointer that crosses row boundaries.

For input 1 1 1 5, the program prints:

Dimensions and entries:
0 0 0 5
